description: Canonical terms for the Report-to-LCA Evidence Engine research proposal.

aliases: 报告到 LCA 证据引擎
keywords.short: An agentic pipeline that turns sustainability reports into LCA-relevant structured evidence.
keywords.definition: A Report-to-LCA Evidence Engine extracts environmental, social and supply-chain evidence from sustainability reports, aligns it to LCA-related schemas, judges applicability, and records provenance for expert audit.

keywords.short: A corporate disclosure document containing environmental, social and governance information.
keywords.definition: A sustainability report is a company-published document that may include emissions, energy, water, waste, supply-chain, workforce, human-rights and climate-target disclosures.

keywords.short: A report-derived evidence object that may support LCA, Scope 3 or S-LCA analysis.
keywords.definition: LCA-relevant evidence is a structured object extracted from a report with indicator, value, unit, boundary, year, source quote, applicability label and review status.

keywords.short: Finding and structuring values, concepts and evidence spans from reports.
keywords.definition: Extraction converts raw report text, tables and figures into structured fields such as indicator, value, unit, year, boundary, quote and confidence.

keywords.short: The exact text, table cell or page region supporting an extracted data point.
keywords.definition: An evidence span is the source location and quote that grounds an extracted indicator so an expert can audit whether the structured output is faithful to the report.

keywords.short: A normalized data record extracted from a report.
keywords.definition: An indicator object contains normalized fields such as company, report year, indicator, value, unit, boundary, source, confidence, applicability and audit flags.

keywords.short: Mapping report language to canonical concepts and relationships.
keywords.definition: Ontology alignment maps varied report expressions such as carbon emissions, operational emissions and Scope 2 market-based emissions to canonical indicators, boundaries and schema fields.

keywords.short: A semantic graph that constrains concept matching and recommendation.
keywords.definition: A knowledge graph links indicators, units, boundaries, reporting frameworks, LCA concepts and aliases so extraction and mapping are more consistent than free-text matching alone.

keywords.short: Using a large model to guide, label, critique or distill smaller models.
keywords.definition: In this proposal, a large model acts as teacher for schema refinement, rationale generation, hard negatives and error diagnosis, while smaller models perform scalable extraction and classification.

keywords.short: A lower-cost model used for high-throughput extraction and classification.
keywords.definition: A small model can be trained or guided to extract spans, classify indicators, normalize units, tag applicability and flag audit risks at lower cost and with more reproducible behavior than a large model alone.

keywords.short: Whether an extracted data point is useful for a specific LCA-related task.
keywords.definition: Applicability classifies report-derived evidence as product-LCA-ready, screening-LCA-ready, corporate-inventory-ready, Scope-3-ready, S-LCA-ready, weak-signal-only or not applicable.

keywords.short: The rate at which unusable evidence is incorrectly marked as LCA-ready.
keywords.definition: False-ready rate measures a dangerous applicability error: a system says a report-derived data point is ready for a rigorous LCA task when expert review says it is not.

keywords.short: A labeled dataset and metric suite for evaluating extraction and applicability.
keywords.definition: The benchmark pairs sustainability report evidence spans with gold labels for extracted fields, concept mappings, applicability classes and audit flags.

keywords.short: How easily an expert can verify an agent output from source evidence.
keywords.definition: Auditability requires every extracted claim to preserve source file, page, quote, method context, confidence, rationale and review status so an expert can accept or correct it efficiently.

keywords.short: The traceable source trail behind an extracted data point.
keywords.definition: Provenance records the document, page, section, quote, table cell, extraction method and reviewer status that support a structured evidence object.

keywords.short: A reviewable signal that a disclosure may be incomplete, inconsistent or weakly evidenced.
keywords.definition: An audit flag marks issues such as missing boundary, missing method, intensity-only disclosure, target without baseline, omitted Scope 3 categories or weak evidence.

keywords.short: A reviewable risk signal, not a final accusation.
keywords.definition: Greenwashing risk in this proposal means evidence-backed flags that a report may overstate sustainability performance, omit key data, use unclear boundaries or emphasize targets without verifiable progress.

keywords.short: Indirect value-chain GHG emissions categories defined by the GHG Protocol.
keywords.definition: Scope 3 emissions include upstream and downstream value-chain categories such as purchased goods, transport, business travel, use of sold products and end-of-life treatment.

aliases: 社会生命周期评价证据
keywords.short: Report evidence relevant to social impacts across stakeholder categories.
keywords.definition: Social LCA evidence includes report disclosures on workers, local communities, society, consumers and value-chain actors that can support S-LCA screening or assessment.

keywords.short: External verification status for reported sustainability information.
keywords.definition: Assurance indicates whether selected sustainability metrics or report sections were externally checked, which affects auditability and confidence in extracted evidence.

keywords.short: Human validation of extraction, applicability and audit flags.
keywords.definition: Expert review checks whether the system's extracted value, concept mapping, applicability label and risk flag are faithful to the report and useful for the research task.
